definition: A simple probabilistic classifier based on applying Bayes' theorem with a strong (naive) assumption of feature independence.
details: Despite its simplifying assumptions, Naive Bayes performs surprisingly well on tasks like text classification and spam filtering, and remains a useful, fast baseline model.

explainer.lead: Naive Bayes is a simple probabilistic classifier that applies Bayes' theorem while assuming features are independent. Despite that strong assumption it performs surprisingly well on text classification and spam filtering and serves as a fast baseline.

tiers.eli5: It's like guessing whether an email is spam by weighing each suspicious word separately, without worrying how the words combine.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers train it by estimating per-feature class probabilities and multiply them at prediction time; a pitfall is that correlated or redundant features violate the independence assumption and can skew the scores.
tiers.paperLevel: Class prediction is the class maximizing P(c) times the product over features of P(x_i | c), by Bayes' theorem with conditional independence of features given the class; the assumption is rarely true in practice.

explainer.example: Given the words in an email, the model multiplies the prior probability of spam by each word's spam-conditional probability and picks whichever class scores higher.
